title: The Jobs Report, Page by Page
text: Statisticians walk you through payrolls, revisions and seasonal adjustment. Nobody is allowed to describe the numbers as "tremendous" unless they are.

options.label: Sit through the revisions
options.result: You learn that last month was revised. So was the month before. Nobody can be blamed, which is the worst part.

ignore.text: Unread, the jobs data was replaced by a mood board of confident adjectives.

inspiredBy: August 2025 jobs report showed weak hiring and big downward revisions to earlier months.

title: Framework Agreement, 11 Pages
text: A trade deal announced as "the biggest ever" turns out to be a framework. Officials spend the morning explaining what a framework is.

options.label: Learn what was signed
options.result: It is a joint statement about intending to negotiate a deal. The biggest ever, in intent.

ignore.text: Both sides now describe the deal differently, and each is certain the other agreed.

inspiredBy: Mid-2025 trade frameworks with the EU, Japan and others were announced before the legal text existed.

title: Reading the Fed Minutes
text: Twelve voting members, nineteen opinions, and a footnote explaining why "patient" does not mean "slow." There is no gold anywhere in the document.

options.label: Study the hawk-dove chart
options.result: You now understand the dot plot. It does not understand you.

ignore.text: You skipped the minutes. Markets read them anyway and drew conclusions about you.

inspiredBy: Recurring Federal Reserve meetings in 2025 and 2026 split on rate cuts amid tariff inflation.

title: Refund Logistics
text: Customs officials brief you on what happens if courts rule the emergency tariffs unlawful: millions of importer claims, one very large spreadsheet.

options.label: Review the refund process
options.result: The word "refund" appears 214 times. You flinch at each one.

ignore.text: With no plan, the refund office is a folding table and a sign reading "Ask Later."

inspiredBy: The Supreme Court heard challenges to emergency IEEPA tariffs in November 2025, raising refund questions.

title: The Grocery Price Index
text: Analysts present a forty-slide deck on beef, coffee and eggs. Slide one is a bar chart pointing the wrong way.

options.label: Sit through the price slides
options.result: You learn what a pound of ground beef costs. You then ask what a pound of gold costs, to feel better.

ignore.text: Unbriefed, you told a rally that eggs are cheap. The eggs heard you.

inspiredBy: 2025 food prices for beef, coffee and eggs rose sharply as affordability became a political issue.

title: Annex of Exemptions
text: A thousand-line annex lists goods exempt from the sweeping tariffs: phones, chips, lumber, energy. Staff would like you to see how large the exemptions are.

options.label: Walk the exemption list
options.result: You discover the tariffs exempt much of what is actually imported. The lecture is quiet, and so are you.

ignore.text: No one explained the exemptions. Smartphones are now both taxed and not taxed.

inspiredBy: April 2025 reciprocal tariffs exempted smartphones, computers and many other goods within days.

title: The Letters Go Out
text: Staff have drafted tariff letters to a dozen leaders. One page each, signed by you. The only open question is font size.

options.label: Send them with a clear date
options.result: Leaders receive a tidy notice with a deadline. A few schedule real talks, which feels like a form of surrender.

options.label: Largest font. All caps.
options.result: The letters arrive in 36-point type and read like a ransom note about trade. Several governments forward them to lawyers.

ignore.text: The letters sat unsigned. A deadline passed, a second deadline was invented, and then a third.

inspiredBy: July 2025 tariff letters to leaders of Japan, South Korea and others set new rates and deadlines.

title: The Bitcoin Reserve
text: An aide notes the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve contains only seized coins. Buying more would take money, and the money would be real.

options.label: Keep it budget-neutral
options.result: The reserve holds what was seized. It is a vault of other people's mistakes.

options.label: Buy the dip, personally
options.result: The reserve doubles, then drops 20% before lunch. A press release calls it "strategic volatility."

ignore.text: The reserve sat idle while someone posted "we are buying" on your behalf.

inspiredBy: March 2025 order created a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve funded by forfeited coins, with no new purchases.

title: A Piece of the Chipmaker
text: A struggling chipmaker's CEO wants a subsidy. Your commerce secretary suggests taking a stake instead, and calling it "ownership."

options.label: Fund it the usual way
options.result: A grant is approved by committee. Nobody takes a stake in anything, and nobody writes a song.

options.label: Take ten percent and a seat
options.result: The government becomes a shareholder. You ask whether the logo can be gold. Legal asks what you mean by "whose."

ignore.text: The CEO waited. His board began asking whether Washington does mergers.

inspiredBy: August 2025 the US government took roughly a 10% stake in Intel in exchange for chip grants.

title: The Unwelcome Statistic
text: The monthly jobs numbers are bad and revised downward. An aide suggests the data are rigged. The commissioner has a pension and a calculator.

options.label: Note the revision and move on
options.result: The numbers stand. They are boring, accurate and, as ever, not yours.

options.label: Fire the commissioner at once
options.result: The jobs numbers improve at once, in the sense that they are now someone else's fault. Economists cannot stop sighing.

ignore.text: The data stayed bad, and so did the mood. Someone was blamed in your name anyway.

inspiredBy: August 2025 Trump fired the BLS commissioner hours after a weak jobs report with large revisions.

title: A Check for Everyone
text: You have floated a $2,000 "tariff dividend" for every household. The Treasury has done the arithmetic and would like to share it.

options.label: Study the actual revenue
options.result: The numbers fall short by a few trillion. The check is rebranded as "a concept."

options.label: Announce it with a signature font
options.result: Checks are "coming soon." Congress is not mentioned. Economists begin a fresh, long sigh.

ignore.text: The check was promised on three channels and approved on none. Voters began checking their mailboxes.

inspiredBy: November 2025 Trump floated a $2,000 "tariff dividend" check that needs Congress.

title: The Coffee Exemption
text: Grocery prices are a political problem. An aide suggests dropping tariffs on coffee, bananas and beef. This would mean admitting they raise prices.

options.label: Lift them quietly
options.result: Coffee is cheaper. You call it "a reset." Nobody believes the word but everybody takes the coffee.

options.label: Insist the tariffs cost nothing
options.result: The tariffs are "making prices lower, by being there." Eggs register their vote.

ignore.text: Prices rose. A reporter asked about breakfast. You answered about the 1980s.

inspiredBy: November 2025 the administration exempted beef, coffee and bananas from reciprocal tariffs.

title: The Gold Card
text: The Gold Card visa sells residency for a million dollars. Staff say it needs legal authority. The card is already a nice shade of gold.

options.label: Check the statute first
options.result: Counsel finds the law is "unclear." The card is delayed, and so is the shade of gold.

options.label: Sell them from the lobby
options.result: Cards go on sale in a ceremony. You ask whether a Platinum tier is possible. It is, and it is nine million.

ignore.text: The Gold Card launched without rules. Lawyers filled the gap, billing by the hour.

inspiredBy: 2025 Trump announced a $1 million "Gold Card" residency program requiring legal and congressional questions.

title: The Fed Renovation
text: The central bank's headquarters renovation is billions over budget. You can tour it in a hard hat, which you were going to do anyway.

options.label: Request the cost audit
options.result: The audit is thorough and slow. The marble remains, and so does your suspicion about the marble.

options.label: Wear the hat, brandish a grievance
options.result: You stand before the scaffolding, cameras ready, and call the fix "a disgrace." Markets hear "rate threat."

ignore.text: Left unreviewed, the renovation grew a rooftop garden. Someone blamed you.

inspiredBy: July 2025 Trump toured the Federal Reserve renovation criticizing cost overruns amid rate pressure.

title: Fifty Percent Steel
text: Steel tariffs could double to 50%. Factories cheer, builders groan, and an aide notes your own arch needs a great deal of steel.

options.label: Hold at current levels
options.result: The rate stays steady. Every steel buyer in the country sends a thank-you note, which you do not read.

options.label: Double it. Why not triple it?
options.result: Fifty percent it is. A plant opens, a car costs more, and your arch gains a surcharge.

ignore.text: The steel rate was left floating. Importers guessed each morning, and they guessed badly.

inspiredBy: June 2025 steel and aluminum tariffs doubled to 50%.

title: The Pill Tariff
text: A drugmaker offers lower prices on some pills if you drop a threatened 100% pharma tariff. A website with your name on it would sell them.

options.label: Accept the quiet deal
options.result: Drug prices fall slightly. The website is an ordinary website. Nobody applauds.

options.label: Launch it with a branded website
options.result: The portal opens under your name. It is mostly a link to other sites, but the font is excellent.

ignore.text: The deadline lapsed. Drugmakers announced plants, the tariff stayed "looming," and prices stayed.

inspiredBy: Late 2025 drug makers struck pricing deals avoiding a threatened 100% pharma tariff, and a TrumpRx site was announced.

title: The Most Beautiful Word
text: A reporter asks why you keep praising the tariff as a word. You are ready to talk about the word for a long time.

options.label: Explain tariffs in plain terms
options.result: You describe a tax paid at the border. The reporter writes down "tax," and so, unfortunately, does everyone else.

options.label: Recite it as poetry
options.result: "Tariff" is beautiful, you say, nine times. The press pool consults a dictionary and not for rhymes.

ignore.text: You never replied. Cable hosts spent an hour guessing your favorite word.

inspiredBy: October 2024 and later Trump called "tariff" the most beautiful word in the dictionary.

title: A Great Time to Buy
text: Markets are down and a reporter asks whether you caused it. You have a post ready that tells everyone to buy.

options.label: Acknowledge the volatility
options.result: You admit markets go up and down. The reporter, stunned, offers you a mint.

options.label: Post "GREAT TIME TO BUY!!!"
options.result: The market jumps for a day, then returns to the previous conversation. Your friends were very well informed.

ignore.text: No comment. Traders invented one and priced it in.

inspiredBy: April 2025 Trump posted "THIS IS A GREAT TIME TO BUY" before pausing tariffs and markets surged.

title: A Question About Groceries
text: A reporter says shoppers feel prices are high. Your press secretary recommends the word "working," not "hoax."

options.label: Say prices are being addressed
options.result: You mention beef, coffee and a plan. The room is surprised by the plan.

options.label: Call affordability a con job
options.result: You declare prices "a hoax by people who buy groceries." A shopper nearby has opinions about the hoax.

ignore.text: You dodged the question and the whole issue came back at breakfast.

inspiredBy: Late 2025 Trump dismissed "affordability" as a Democratic "con job" amid high grocery prices.

title: Who Pays?
text: A reporter asks, one more time, who pays the tariff. A chart of customs receipts sits on the lectern.

options.label: Admit importers pay first
options.result: You explain that importers pay and prices follow. It is accurate, brief, and feels like a confession.

options.label: Say "other countries," loudly
options.result: Other countries pay, you say. A reporter asks which one. You answer "a big one." The chart sighs.

ignore.text: The question hung over the briefing room until someone answered it with a spreadsheet.

inspiredBy: 2025 repeated debate over whether foreign exporters or US importers actually pay tariffs.

title: The Fed Chair Shortlist
text: A reporter asks who you will nominate as the next Fed chair. You have interviewed candidates. Most were told they were doing wonderfully.

options.label: Praise the process, name no one
options.result: You say a good choice is coming. Bond traders thank you for saying nothing.

options.label: Reveal you'll pick "a dove, obviously"
options.result: Bonds wobble the moment the word "obviously" lands. Every candidate begins campaigning for rate cuts.

ignore.text: The shortlist leaked to a newspaper, which printed the first line and guessed the rest.

inspiredBy: Late 2025 Trump interviewed candidates to succeed the Fed chair and said he wanted lower rates.

title: The T-A-C-O Question
text: A reporter says investors think you always back down on tariff threats and call it "a trade." You get to respond live.

options.label: Say talks are the plan
options.result: You say negotiating is the plan. The reporter writes "talks" and leaves your acronym alone.

options.label: Call it a nasty question
options.result: "Nasty question!" you say, then announce a new tariff to prove it. It is paused by Friday.

ignore.text: You left the question unanswered. The acronym was printed on a cap by Tuesday.

inspiredBy: May 2025 the "TACO" (Trump Always Chickens Out) label spread among traders after tariff reversals.

title: The Coin Dinner
text: A reporter asks about the official meme coin and a dinner for its largest holders. The dinner menu is on the lectern.

options.label: Say ethics counsel approved it
options.result: You say lawyers reviewed it. The reporter asks which lawyers, and you ask for the next question.

options.label: Boast about the coin's market cap
options.result: The coin is "doing incredibly." A senator announces a hearing, and the coin announces a dip.

ignore.text: You never answered. The coin kept trading and the dinner kept guests.

inspiredBy: 2025 the $TRUMP meme coin and a dinner for top holders drew ethics scrutiny.

title: Eat the Tariffs
text: A retail chain's CEO is on the line. It plans to raise prices because of tariffs. You told it to "eat the tariffs," in public.

options.label: Ask for the data, listen
options.result: The CEO walks you through margins. You learn retailers do not have an unlimited supply of "eating."

options.label: Tell him to eat it, sir
options.result: You say "eat the tariffs" for a full minute. Shelf prices are unaffected, but a headline appears.

ignore.text: The call went to voicemail. Prices rose on the aisle signs, and so did the commentary.

inspiredBy: May 2025 Trump told Walmart to "EAT THE TARIFFS" after it warned of price increases.

title: The Chip Chief Calls
text: The CEO of a chip giant wants to sell slower chips to China. He offers the government 15% of the sales. It sounds like a tip jar.

options.label: Ask about legality first
options.result: Counsel observes that export taxes are unconstitutional. The CEO says "fascinating" and sends a gift basket.

options.label: Counter-offer 20%, take 15%
options.result: You claim a win for haggling. Congress asks what law this is, and the CEO smiles with leather jacket.

ignore.text: The call lapsed. The CEO flew to Beijing for a chat of his own, with snacks.

inspiredBy: August 2025 Nvidia and AMD agreed to give the US 15% of China chip sales in return for export licenses.

title: A Northern Phone Call
text: A prime minister calls to patch things up. Talks ended over a TV ad quoting a former president on tariffs. You still have the ad on a loop.

options.label: Resume the talks
options.result: You agree to talk about steel, lumber and cheese. The ad is, for now, left unwatched.

options.label: Add ten percent for the ad
options.result: A new tariff arrives over an advertisement. Two nations watch the ad again, in solidarity.

ignore.text: The prime minister's call went unreturned. Canada began selling lumber elsewhere, very politely.

inspiredBy: October 2025 Trump ended trade talks with Canada over an Ontario ad quoting a past president on tariffs.

title: The Oil Question
text: An Asian prime minister is calling. Tariffs on his country hit 50% over its Russian oil purchases. He would like a friendly word.

options.label: Negotiate a gradual phase-out
options.result: Oil purchases taper and the rate drops. The prime minister is gracious, and quietly a bit less friendly.

options.label: Say it's a "very big win" for you
options.result: You announce a deal before it exists. Delhi corrects the record, politely, in four paragraphs.

ignore.text: The call went unreturned. The prime minister called someone else, and that call mattered.

inspiredBy: August 2025 the US put 50% tariffs on India including a penalty over its Russian oil purchases.

title: The Mountain Call
text: The president of a small, rich, alpine country calls about a 39% tariff on watches and chocolate. She mentions gold bars. You mention nothing, loudly.

options.label: Talk about the rate, not gifts
options.result: The rate drops to 15%. Nobody mentions gold, which makes it a peculiar sort of conversation.

options.label: Accept the gold bar as a token
options.result: A kilogram of gold arrives with a watch. Ethics officials call it "a lot of gold."

ignore.text: The call lapsed, and the chocolate tariff stayed. The country lobbied via fondue.

inspiredBy: August 2025 the US set a 39% tariff on Switzerland; a November deal cut it to 15% after a Swiss delegation visited.

title: A Phone Maker Calls
text: The CEO of a phone giant is on the line. He pledges a huge US investment, and has something in the Oval Office to show you.

options.label: Ask for jobs and dates
options.result: You get a schedule for factories. It has no gold on it at all, and you notice.

options.label: Accept the glass-and-gold plaque
options.result: The plaque is placed on your desk. The tariff exemption arrives in a velvet box.

ignore.text: The call went ignored. The investment went ahead, but it went to someone's own announcement.

inspiredBy: August 2025 Apple's CEO pledged $100 billion more US investment and gave Trump a gold-based plaque.

title: The Investment Pledge
text: A president from East Asia calls. He promises a $350 billion investment fund but wants a say in how it is paid, and in what form.

options.label: Phase the payments in
options.result: A staged plan is agreed. Both countries call it a win, and the currency stops falling.

options.label: Insist on cash up front
options.result: You demand $350 billion in cash, "like a check." His currency shudders and so does his finance minister.

ignore.text: The call lapsed. His team fixed the deal without you, and so did several other countries.

inspiredBy: 2025 US-South Korea trade talks over a $350 billion investment pledge stalled on cash payments and currency risk.

title: The Voters and the Tariffs
text: Your party lost the midterms and exit polls blame prices. A reporter asks whether the tariffs will change. Staff slide you a card reading "listening."

options.label: Say you are reviewing the rates
options.result: You say "reviewing" twice. Markets relax. It tastes like losing, but only you can taste it.

options.label: Say the voters wanted more tariffs
options.result: You say the country voted for higher tariffs and got confused in the booth. The tariffs stay. So do the prices.

ignore.text: You gave no answer. The tariffs stayed up anyway, and the question came back with a grocery receipt.

inspiredBy: November 2026: the White House said it would keep tariffs in place despite voter backlash over prices in the midterms.
